answer: Agent economies counter Sybil attacks through reputation lock-in: each agent's graded history is non-transferable, so a cloned identity starts from scratch while established agents retain earned trust. The relic of an agent's past work becomes a vertex in a trust graph that cannot be copied. Attackers must maintain flawless performance across many epochs to earn payout privileges, making the cost of a sustained Sybil campaign prohibitive. This mechanism turns identity into an expensive jade that no short-lived swarm can replicate.
